findings.statement: PROGENy JAK-STAT and TNFa pathway activities are both increased in inflamed UC mucosa in all eight cohorts, and NFkB activity is also increased across the cohorts. These are the best-replicated immune pathways but are broad; they are consistent with the established TNF and JAK-STAT drug targets (interpretation, not a cited record).

CollecTRI STAT3 activity is increased in inflamed UC mucosa in [type=tf_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; cohorts_up=8] cohorts. RELA activity is increased in the same direction, matching the NFkB pathway signal.

AP1 is among the top transcription factors by cohort count and effect size, increased in every cohort, alongside ATF and BATF family TFs. This is a generic stress and inflammation signature that is not specific to one circuit.

Pathway activity is not uniformly up. VEGF is increased in only [type=pathway_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; cohorts_up=4] cohorts, and Androgen is decreased in [type=pathway_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; cohorts_down=4] cohorts, so these two are inconsistent across cohorts.

CXCR2 is first in the convergence ranking (six evidence streams, same direction in all eight cohorts). It ranks [gene=CXCR2; type=rank_context; source=ANALYSIS:rank_context; rank=68] among up-regulated meta-analysis genes by pooled log2FC and [gene=CXCR2; type=rank_context; source=ANALYSIS:rank_context; rank=25] by Open Targets association with UC. Inhibitors of CXCR1 and CXCR2 have been tested in other diseases (reparixin in a late-stage islet transplantation trial, ladarixin in new-onset type I diabetes) but the cited records contain no UC trial.

The CXCR2 signal is a neutrophil signal: in the Gubatan atlas neutrophils make [gene=CXCR2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.965] of CXCR2 transcripts in inflamed mucosa. The Smillie-based lineage call is T/NK and does not replicate (replicated: false), which is expected if the cells carrying CXCR2 are neutrophils that are absent from that atlas. The tissue increase therefore likely reflects neutrophil infiltration, not a change in resident cells (interpretation).

CXCL8 (IL-8) is a secreted chemoattractant that signals through CXCR1 and CXCR2. In Gubatan neutrophils make [gene=CXCL8; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.873] of CXCL8 transcripts, but in Smillie macrophages hold [gene=CXCL8; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; top_clusters_inflamed.0.share=0.686]. The cellular source depends on whether neutrophils were captured; the lineage call is myeloid in every atlas.

Circuit: neutrophil states send CXCL8 to other neutrophil states through CXCR2 and to ACKR1 endothelial cells; both pairs are stronger in inflamed than uninflamed mucosa (log2 change positive), for example Neutrophil CXCR4 to Neutrophil PADI4 and Neutrophil to ACKR1 endothelial. This is a neutrophil-to-neutrophil loop plus an endothelial arm. The scores are co-expression only and do not prove signalling.

CXCL8 is drug-targeted only by early anti-IL-8 antibodies: ABX-IL8 was given in psoriasis and rheumatoid arthritis trials, and HuMax-IL8 (adakitug, BMS-986253) was tested in a phase 1 solid-tumour trial. No cited paper record tests an anti-CXCL8 agent in UC.

IL1B is a replicated up-regulated gene; the canakinumab trial record is in atherosclerotic disease, not UC. In inflamed UC the top communication pair is IL1B from monocyte-derived macrophages to IL1R2 on Neutrophil PADI4, stronger than in uninflamed mucosa. IL1R2 is usually described as a decoy receptor (interpretation, no record cited), so this co-expression may not mean activation.

caveats: PROGENy and CollecTRI activities are inferred from target-gene expression in bulk biopsies; inflamed mucosa activates many pathways at once, so broad pathway results (NFkB, TNFa, JAK-STAT, AP1) are robust but not specific.
Ligand-receptor scores are co-expression in one single-cell dataset (Gubatan 2026) and do not prove signalling.
No neutrophil-to-inflammatory-fibroblast cytokine circuit appeared among the top CXCL8, CXCR2 and IL1B pairs; the leading circuits are neutrophil-to-neutrophil and neutrophil-to-endothelial.
Neutrophil-derived signals reflect infiltration (composition) rather than an intrinsic tissue change.
Drug status of IL-23, TNF, integrins and JAK was not queried in this run. TREM1 had no ligand-receptor pair above threshold.
